chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Shuʿayb, who said:

I asked Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about a man who married a woman who already had a husband. He said: “They are to be separated.” I said: Is there beating upon him? He said: “No, why should he be beaten?” So I came out from his presence, and Abū Baṣīr was opposite the water-spout. I informed him of the issue and the answer, so he said to me: Where am I? I said: Opposite the water-spout. He said: Then he raised his hand and said: By the Lord of this House, or by the Lord of this Kaʿbah, I indeed heard Jaʿfar saying: “ʿAlī عليه السلام judged concerning a man who married a woman who had a husband, so he stoned the woman and struck the man with the hadd. Then he said: If I had known that you knew, I would have smashed your head with stones.” Then he said: “How greatly I fear that his knowledge may not have been given to him.”

Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan said: What Abū Baṣīr heard from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام does not contradict what Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام gave as a legal ruling, because he عليه السلام only denied the hadd from him because he did not know that she had a husband. As for the one whom Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام struck, that bears two possibilities: one of them is that he struck him because of his knowledge that she had a husband, and Abū Baṣīr has narrated that in what Yūnus narrated from him, and we have already mentioned it. The second is that, due to his predominant assumption that she had a husband, he was negligent in investigating her condition, so he struck him as taʿzīr, and there is nothing in the report stating that he struck him with the complete hadd. And his statement عليه السلام, “If I had known that you knew, I would have smashed your head with stones,” means: if you had known with certain knowledge that she had a husband, I would have done that to you. And it is also possible that what is meant is that the man was under suspicion regarding his having contracted marriage with her, while he had not actually contracted it, and he had no proof of marriage; so at that point the hadd was established against him on account of the suspicion. That is indicated by what he narrated:

key_terms.زَوْجٌ: a lawful husband already bound to the woman
key_terms.يُفَرَّقُ: they are to be separated legally

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a man who marries a woman who already has a husband in Shiʿi hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the legal consequences for a man who marries a woman already bound in marriage, distinguishing between deliberate knowledge and lack of knowledge. It also includes Shaykh al-Ṭūsī’s reconciliation of apparently differing reports by explaining that punishment varies according to certainty, suspicion, and the presence or absence of proof.
